The son will most likely prevail, because he was an intended third-party beneficiary named in the written contract. The "valid assignment" theory is wrong, since the landscaper never assigned anything to him. My earlier answer, that he loses because the parties modified the contract before his rights vested, rested on the Restatement vesting rule. That rule doesn't fit the answer choices given, so I'm changing my answer.

CONFIDENCE: 62
